fields.subnational_unit: Lowndes County, Alabama (Black Belt; unincorporated areas)
fields.population: households in unincorporated rural Lowndes County served by the Black Belt Unincorporated Wastewater Program (BBUWP); program staff, installers and community members
fields.sample_size: qualitative case study of one program: operational records (inspections, repairs, maintenance schedules), semi-structured interviews with BBUWP staff, installers and community members (number not stated), field observations, and prior program evaluations
fields.effect_measure: qualitative description of maintenance and management strategies for decentralised onsite wastewater systems; no quantitative measure
fields.effect_estimate: BBUWP retains responsibility for oversight and maintenance of grant-funded onsite systems, functioning as a decentralised utility. Strategies: standardised system selection and type-specific preventive maintenance (conventional, engineered, advanced engineered closed-loop systems); local workforce development with technical schools to fill the shortage of certified Level II installers; a centralised asset database; zones reused for maintenance routing; diversified funding (membership models, reserves, grants). The author reports fewer failures and higher community trust without presenting data. Context: dense clay soils, no sewer in unincorporated areas, limited regulatory enforcement capacity, illegal straight piping.
fields.model_type: qualitative case study of an organisation
fields.study_design: qualitative single-programme case study (conference paper); author affiliated with a consultancy that works with the programme
